name: Jaguar E Type | www.vecarz.com
author: vecarz
description:
showcase website: https://www.vecarz.com/blog/jaguar-e-type-4-2-1967

This is an exhilarating E-Type model, with sleek, flowing lines that seem to say, “I’m the embodiment of speed and passion.” But as you grip the wheel, you can’t help but laugh, “The polygons on this windshield must be fewer than the cars I drew in elementary school!” The low-poly modeling makes this E-Type look like it just drove out of a PS1 game, awkwardly stepping into the modern 3D world.  

Even if the windshield seems pixelated, the long hood and iconic curvy rear still captivate. This car feels like a British gentleman in a worn-out suit – frayed but effortlessly charming. Fixing it might be tough, but as they say, “People don’t buy cars with logic; they buy them with passion.”  

No matter how Minecraft-like that windshield is, I’d still take it for a spin. The E-Type will always be worth the adventure.
![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65d4bfc10f577ede0713402d/677d357a2f985543df2de2d4_EtypeBanner.jpg)

name: 1971 Jaguar E-Type Series 3 V12 Roadster
author: Ddiaz Design
description:
Repositorio de modelos 3D de Ddiaz Design

![](https://images.collectingcars.com/021202/mainimage.jpg?w=1263&fit=fillmax&crop=edges&auto=format,compress&cs=srgb&q=85)

A new 5.3 L 12-cylinder Jaguar V12 engine was introduced, with uprated brakes and standard power steering. The short wheelbase FHC body style was discontinued and the V12 was available only as a convertible and 2+2 coupé. The convertible used the longer-wheelbase 2+2 floorplan. It is easily identifiable by the large cross-slatted front grille, flared wheel arches and a badge on the rear that proclaims it to be a V12. There were also a very limited number of 4.2 litre six-cylinder Series 3 E-Types built. These were featured in the initial sales literature. It is believed these are the rarest of all E-Types of any remaining.

name: Jaguar Type E
author: L'Atelier 5D
description: The Jaguar E-Type, or the Jaguar XK-E for the North American market, is a British sports car that was manufactured by Jaguar Cars Ltd between 1961 and 1974. Its combination of beauty, high performance, and competitive pricing established the model as an icon of the motoring world. The E-Type's claimed 150 mph (241 km/h) top speed, sub-7-second 0 to 60 mph (97 km/h) acceleration, unitary construction, disc brakes, rack-and-pinion steering, and independent front and rear suspension distinguished the car and spurred industry-wide changes. The E-Type was based on Jaguar's D-Type racing car, which had won the 24 Hours of Le Mans for three consecutive years beginning in 1955, and employed what was, for the early 1960s, a novel racing design principle, with a front subframe carrying the engine, front suspension and front bodywork bolted directly to the body tub. No ladder frame chassis, as was common at the time, was needed and as such the first cars weighed only 1315 kg (2900 lb).

name: 1984 Ferrari 288 GTO
author: Res1n
description:
*The 1984 Ferrari 288 GTO is an iconic halo supercar built for canceled Group B racing. Powered by a 2.8-liter twin-turbocharged V8 producing 400 horsepower, it reaches 0–60 mph in roughly 4.9 seconds with a top speed of 189 mph. Ferrari produced 272 units between 1984 and 1987.*

**Engineering and Design**
Engine: Longitudinal 2,855 cc V8 with twin IHI turbochargers and Behr intercoolers.
Body Construction: Lightweight composite panels utilizing fiberglass, Kevlar, carbon-fiber, and Nomex.
Chassis: Tubular steel frame featuring a longer wheelbase and widened track compared to the 308 GTB.
Interior: Minimalist, driver-focused cabin with leather trim, classic analog gauges, and a gated manual shifter.


Credit: @niev

name: 2017 Ferrari J50
author: Res1n
description:
*The 2017 Ferrari J50 is an ultra-exclusive, mid-engine targa roadster built in a strictly limited run of only 10 units to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Ferrari in Japan.*

**Key Specifications**
Engine: 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8
Power: 690 hp (681 bhp / 507 kW)
Torque: 560 lb-ft (760 Nm)
Drivetrain: Rear-wheel drive (RWD) with a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission
Performance: 0–100 km/h (0–62 mph) in roughly 2.8 seconds; top speed of 335 km/h (208 mph)

**Design & Features**
Base: Developed by Maranello's Special Projects department using the Ferrari 488 Spider as its foundation.
Body Style: Features a two-piece carbon-fiber hard targa top that stows behind the seats, harking back to classic Ferrari roadsters of the 1970s and 1980s.
Aero & Styling: Incorporates a futuristic "helmet visor" window graphic, a transparent polycarbonate engine cover framed by dual roll hoops, and a jet-afterburner-inspired rear diffuser.


Credit: @niev

name: 1986 Ferrari Testarossa
author: Res1n
description:
*The legendary 1986 Ferrari Testarossa is powered by a 4.9-liter flat-12 engine producing 385–390 hp. It accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h (0–62 mph) in 5.2 seconds and reaches a top speed of 290 km/h (180 mph). The car features rear-wheel drive and a 5-speed manual transmission.*

**Design & Features**
Styled by the famous Pininfarina design house.
Iconic side strakes ("cheese graters") running along the doors.
Ultra-wide rear track for dramatic, aggressive proportions.
Retro pop-up headlights.
Dual side-mounted radiators to prevent cabin overheating.

**Engine Specifications**
Type: 48-valve flat-12 (180° V12).
Displacement: 4,942 cc.
Power: 385–390 hp @ 6,300 rpm.
Torque: 490 Nm (361 lb-ft) @ 4,500 rpm.

**Performance**
Top Speed: 290 km/h (180 mph).
0–100 km/h (0–62 mph): 5.2–5.3 seconds.
Quarter Mile: ~13.5 seconds.


Credit: @niev

name: 1986 Ferrari 308 GTS
author: Res1n
description:
*The 1986 Ferrari 308 GTS (Quattrovalvole) is an iconic mid-engine, two-seater Targa-topped sports car powered by a 2.9-liter 32-valve V8 engine producing roughly 240 horsepower. It features a transverse 5-speed manual gated shifter, Pininfarina styling, and a top speed of around 155 mph. 1986 marked the final year of production for the legendary 308 series before it was fully succeeded by the Ferrari 328.*

**Engine and Performance Specs**
Engine Type: 2.9 L (2,926 cc) naturally aspirated 90-degree V8
Valvetrain: DOHC with 4 valves per cylinder (Quattrovalvole)
Power Output: 240 hp @ 7,000 rpm (US version slightly lower due to emissions)
Torque: 186 lb-ft @ 5,000 rpm
Transmission: 5-speed manual transaxle with classic open-gated shifter
0–60 mph (0–100 km/h): ~6.1 seconds
Top Speed: ~155 mph (250 km/h)


Credit: @niev

name: 1965 Ferrari 330 GT
author: Res1n
description:
*The 1965 Ferrari 330 GT 2+2 is a classic luxury grand tourer powered by a 4.0-liter Colombo V12 engine producing 300 horsepower. Featuring bodywork designed by Pininfarina, 1965 marked a major transition year as production shifted from the four-headlamp Series I ("Chinese eyes") to the dual-headlamp Series II layout.*

**Specifications and Performance**
Engine: 3,967 cc Colombo V12 with three Weber carburetors
Power: 300 hp at 6,600 rpm
Transmission: 4-speed manual with overdrive or later 5-speed manual
Top Speed: ~245 km/h (152 mph)

**Design Evolution in 1965**
Series I (1963–1965): Distinctive quad-headlight arrangement that earned the affectionate nickname "Chinese eyes".
Interim / Series II (1965–1967): Replaced the quad headlights with a cleaner dual-headlight setup, upgraded to a 5-speed gearbox, and added dual-circuit brakes.


Credit: @niev

name: Abandoned Car - Ferrari Amalfi

description: The McLaren Solus GT is a limited-production track-only mid-engined sports car manufactured by McLaren Automotive. The car is the sixth addition in the McLaren Ultimate Series, joining the McLaren F1, McLaren P1, McLaren Senna, McLaren Speedtail, and McLaren Elva.The 5.2 L (320 cu in) V10 is a Judd-derived block, which McLaren claims produces in excess of 840 PS (829 hp; 618 kW) and 650 N⋅m (479 lb⋅ft) with a redline of 10,000 rpm The engine has individual barrel-driven throttle bodies, with gear-driven camshafts, bespoke crank, intake and exhaust systems Power is sent from the engine to the rear wheels via a Le Mans Prototype-spec 7-speed sequential gearbox, and McLaren claims that the car will do 0–100 km/h (0–62 mph) in 2.5 seconds, with a top speed in excess of 322 km/h (200 mph) The gearbox is of aluminium-magnesium construction and consists of straight-cut gears, with a carbon fibre clutch, and with the engine the two will act as stressed members.

name: 2015 McLaren 650S GT3
author: Dave Love SketchFab
description:
The McLaren 650S GT3 is a dedicated racing car designed and manufactured by and its motorsport division, McLaren GT. Introduced for the 2015 global sports car racing season, the vehicle was built to comply with the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) GT3 regulations. It directly succeeded the McLaren 12C GT3, addressing its predecessor's cooling, aerodynamics, and drivability limitations.

During its competitive lifecycle, the 650S GT3 achieved prominent success across international sports car championships, including the Blancpain GT Series, Pirelli World Challenge, and the Australian GT Championship, highlighted by an outright victory at the 2016 Liqui Moly Bathurst 12 Hour.

The 650S GT3 is built upon the production road car's carbon-fiber "MonoCell" passenger tub, which provides extreme rigidity and lightweight structural properties. Aluminum subframes are attached to the front and rear of the tub to carry the suspension and powertrain components.

description:
Repositorio de modelos 3D de Ddiaz Design

![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c1/2022_Lotus_Emira.jpg)

The Lotus Emira has been developed on a new lightweight bonded aluminium chassis, technology pioneered by Lotus and which remains an intrinsic part of the company's sports car DNA. That innovative vehicle architecture is wrapped with a bold and sculpted design using cues clearly developed from the Evija. Key dimensions of the Emira are length 4,412mm; width 1,895mm; height 1,225mm; and wheelbase 2,575mm.

description: The Lotus Evija is an all-electric sports car known for its exceptional power and exclusivity. With over 2,000 horsepower from four electric motors, it accelerates incredibly fast. Its aerodynamic design enhances performance, and rapid charging gets the battery to 80% in about 18 minutes. This limited-edition car combines advanced technology with a focus on lightweight materials, showcasing a new era of high-performance electric vehicles.
